title: SBOM as a Dependency Tree Explorer
description: Interactive vis-network graph of a realistic CycloneDX SBOM for a small web application. Click any component to highlight its path from the root, filter to vulnerable-only or direct-only dependencies, and inspect version, license, hash, and listed CVEs in a side panel.
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: cybersecurity

educational.topic: Software Bill of Materials (SBOM) and dependency-tree vulnerability tracing
learningObjectives: Locate a vulnerable component in a dependency tree given a published CVE.
Identify the dependency path from the root application to a transitive dependency.
Distinguish direct from transitive dependencies and explain why transitive risk is easy to miss.
educational.prerequisites: Basic understanding of software packages and that applications reuse third-party libraries.

pedagogical.modelType: interactive dependency graph with filters and detail panel
controls: Search box: find component by name
Click a node: highlight path from root and show details
pedagogical.assessment: Given a CVE published against a transitive dependency (e.g., log4js@2.4.0 or follow-redirects), students locate the component and trace its path back to my-web-app.
misconceptionsAddressed: Believing only direct dependencies introduce risk.
Assuming a vulnerable component is always one the team chose to install.
